issues.description: The problem statement / UML specifies Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning String, and the template code expects calling messageOnFeed() to produce a printable String. The solution repository instead defines messageOnFeed() to return a custom FeedResponse type (and Pig/Seal return FeedResponse instances). This return-type mismatch changes the public API students must implement and introduces an unexpected helper class (FeedResponse) not mentioned in the specification, which can confuse students and block straightforward implementations that follow the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of messageOnFeed() consistent with the problem statement and template. Either (A) change the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (and update Seal/Pig/Goat accordingly, removing or not relying on FeedResponse), or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly specify and document the FeedResponse return type and include FeedResponse in the exercise description. Prefer option A to match the UML/specification that students see.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String (messageOnFeed():String), but the solution repository changes the method signature to return a FeedResponse object (public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed()). This divergence of the return type for the same conceptual API (the feeding message) creates a mapping mismatch: students reading the problem/template expect to implement/consume a String, while the solution introduces a new type (FeedResponse) and wraps the message. This is likely unintentional and forces students to reconcile two different API contracts for the same concept.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API across artifacts. Preferably change the solution to match the problem/template: make Animal.messageOnFeed() return a String (public abstract String messageOnFeed()), and update Pig, Seal, and Goat to return the specified String messages. Remove or adapt the FeedResponse class if present, or alternatively update the problem statement and template to explicitly require FeedResponse if that wrapper type is intentional.
